svg.title: Conjugate Priors vs MCMC
svg.desc: A conjugate prior gives the posterior in closed form but applies narrowly; MCMC sidesteps the normalizing constant and approximates the posterior with draws, but needs convergence diagnostics.
svg.text: Writing the posterior down vs sampling it
Exists only as a set of draws
means the draws aren't the posterior
Update the parameters and the posterior appears
Prior and posterior share a family — one formula ends the computation
The posterior as a histogram of draws
Means and quantiles come from draws, with no density
Step outside the list and the closed form is gone
The chain must mix over the posterior
Only post-convergence draws count as posterior samples
A conjugate prior hands you the posterior, but only for a narrow class of models.
MCMC fits almost any model, but the posterior is known only through draws, so it needs diagnostics.
The integral in the denominator blocks it — MCMC only
compares posterior ratios, so it never needs that integral
Next: how those draws are actually produced — Metropolis-Hastings vs Gibbs.
